This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant-Insurance Company challenging the award dated 29.07.2019 passed by the learned Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District Vidisha (M.P.) in Claim Case No.
78/2018, whereby compensation has been awarded to the claimant.

sentences.text: The appellant seeks reduction of the amount of compensation so awarded.
2. The date of the accident, the finding of negligence, and the liability of the Insurance Company are not in dispute.

The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality,
as the same have not been assailed in the present appeal.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company, while assailing the impugned award,
submitted that respondent No.1/claimant is the daughter of deceased Smt. Arti Richhariya and the sister of deceased Shri Amit Richhariya.
It is contended that from the face of the record, it is evident that the claimant was not dependent upon the earnings of the deceased persons.

It is further submitted that the claimant is a married daughter of deceased Smt. Arti Richhariya and a married sister of deceased Shri Amit Richhariya, and is residing separately with her husband and children.
Therefore, she was not dependent upon the income of the deceased in any manner.
Despite this, the Claims Tribunal has wrongly assessed and awarded compensation, which is impermissible in the eyes of law and deserves to be set aside.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.1/claimant supported the impugned award and placed reliance upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Birender and Others , reported in 2020 Supreme (SC) 25, wherein it has been held that major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on deceased, would be still covered by expression "legal representative" of deceased and entitle to receive compensation under the MACT Act, 1988 does not cease because NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4529 3 MA-6302-2019 of absence of dependency of concerned legal representative.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Birender and Others , reported in 2020 Supreme (SC) 25
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
It is undisputed that respondent No.1, who is the claimant before the Claims Tribunal, is the married daughter of deceased Smt. Arti Richhariya and the sister of deceased Shri Amit Richhariya.
8. From the perusal of the record, it is further evident that the claimant has been residing separately with her husband and children.
Her husband is employed as a Clerk in the Regional Transport Office (RTO), Bhopal, and was earning approximately Rs.19,900/- per month at the relevant time.
The claimant was residing with her family at Guna.
In view of the aforesaid facts, it is manifest that the claimant was living separately from the deceased persons and was being maintained by her husband, who is a salaried government employee.
Thus, it is clear that the claimant was not dependent upon the income of either of the deceased.
Therefore, citation Birender (Supra) produced by claimant is not applicable in her case.

9. In the case of Amrit Bhanu Shali and others Vs National Insurance Co. Ltd.
and others, 2012 ACJ 2002 in para No. 16 has been held as under :-
Admittedly both the parents, Ist appellant- Amrit Bhanu Shali (father) and 2nd appellant- Smt. Sarlaben (mother) have been held to be dependents of deceased- Ritesh Bhanu Shali and, therefore, the Tribunal held that the Ist appellant and 2nd appellant have the right to get the compensation.

sentences.text: she is not found to be dependent upon the deceased.

Thus, both the parents being dependents, i.e., father and the mother, the Tribunal rightly restricted the 'personal and living expenses' of the deceased to 50% and contribution to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4529 4 MA-6302-2019 the family was required to be taken as 50% as per the decision of this Court in the case of Sarla Verma, 2009 ACJ 198 (SC)
10.

In view of the aforesaid legal position, it is evident that a married daughter living separately and maintained by her earning husband cannot be treated as a dependent upon her deceased mother or brother.
In the present case, the claimant's husband was earning a substantial amount as a government servant, and therefore, the claimant was not dependent upon the deceased persons in any manner.
11. This Court is of the considered view that although the claimant is a legal representative of the deceased persons, she was neither wholly nor partially dependent upon them.
Consequently, the Claims Tribunal committed an error in treating the claimant as a dependent and awarding compensation on that basis.

12. However, the claimant, being a legal representative, is entitled to compensation under the conventional heads, namely, no-fault liability, loss of estate, funeral expenses, and consortium, as permissible under law.

13. In respect of the death of Smt. Arti Richhariya, the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.
40,000/- under the head of consortium, Rs. 30,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expenses,
and Rs. 50,000/- towards no- fault liability.

14. In respect of the death of Shri Amit Richhariya, the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.
30,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and Rs. 50,000/- towards no-fault liability.

15. Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case is Rs. 2,00,000/-
as against Rs. 24,42,600/- awarded by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4529 5 MA-6302-2019 Claims Tribunal.
16. Accordingly, the compensation amount is reduced from Rs. 24,42,600/- to Rs. 2,00,000/-.
The said amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
17. All other findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal shall remain undisturbed.
The Insurance Company shall be entitled to recover the excess amount, if any, already deposited, from the Claims Tribunal in accordance with law.

18. In view of the foregoing discussion, the miscellaneous appeal filed by the Insurance Company stands disposed of accordingly (HIRDESH) JUDGE Prachi United India Insurance Company Ltd. ... vs Smt. Sapna Dubey on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81207665/
